title: After amrit
hookLine: a new beginning, not the end of learning
tomorrow: Simran's decided: not yet. so is she less of a Sikh?

cards: An alarm set for early. Snoozed once, then twice, then the sun is up and the quiet hour is gone. Jasleen texts Simran a single word: ruined.
She took amrit on Sunday. On Tuesday she slept straight through her morning Nitnem for the first time. Now she's sure she's broken it already, two days in, and maybe she was never ready at all.
Simran stares at the word on her screen. She has no idea what to send back.

teach.h: A NEW FAMILY, A NEW HOME.
teach.b: Here's what the Sikh code of conduct says right after the ceremony, and it's the answer for Jasleen. The newly initiated are told who their family is now. Their father is Guru Gobind Singh.
Their mother is Mata Sahib Kaur. Their home is Anandpur Sahib.
That's the language of a birth, not a graduation. Amrit isn't a diploma for someone who's done learning.
It's being born into a family where the learning starts, and newborns don't get everything right in their first week. The code expects stumbles, too.

When an amritdhari Sikh breaks the rehat, there's a way back: go before five Sikhs, say it plainly, and accept a tankhah, a penance such as extra prayer or seva. The door back in is built into the path.
And the Granth is honest about all of us.
On ang 61, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: everyone makes mistakes; only the Guru and the Creator never err. A missed morning isn't one of the four things avoided.
It's a missed morning. The rhythm is still the goal, and tomorrow's dawn still comes. So Simran types: you're two days old. babies sleep in. get up tomorrow and start again.
Jasleen sends back a laughing face, and then: ok. tomorrow.

how: After the ceremony the five explain the rehat and name the Khalsa's spiritual father, mother and home. An amritdhari Sikh who breaks the rehat can go before five Sikhs and accept a tankhah, a penance.

o: a new beginning, when the learning really starts
the moment a Sikh can no longer make mistakes
a graduation after the learning is all done

games.q: after the ceremony — tap the pairs.
p: the father named for the initiated
the mother named for the initiated
the home named for the initiated
a penance: the way back in

s: after amrit, one missed morning prayer means retaking the ceremony
a missed morning isn't one of the four things avoided; you pick the rhythm up again.
the code names a spiritual father and mother for the newly initiated
Guru Gobind Singh and Mata Sahib Kaur, with Anandpur Sahib as home.
amrit marks the end of a Sikh's learning
it's the language of a birth: the learning starts there.

games.q: your friend started a new job and made a mistake in week one. she wants to quit before anyone notices. going by today, what helps?
o: it's a beginning, not a finish line: own it and pick it up tomorrow.
quit now; if week one went wrong, it was never meant to work.
hide it and hope nobody ever finds out.
games.why: amrit is a birth, not a graduation, and the path has a way back built in. everyone makes mistakes, says ang 61.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you meant to start and let slide: a habit, a call, a page of reading. Do the smallest possible piece of it now, even just one line or one stretch. Then sit, and let it count as day one again.

wordCard.voice: After amrit. A birth into the Khalsa family, where the learning begins rather than ends.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: tankhah, a penance accepted after a breach of the rehat.

carryVoice: Keep this one: a new beginning, and missed mornings come with a way back in. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sikh Rehat Maryada, section on the amrit ceremony (the spiritual father, mother and home named) and on tankhah (penance for breaches), paraphrased
Ang 61 (Sri Raag, Guru Nanak: bhulan andar sabh ko abhul guru kartar), paraphrased
